subject: Subprocessor delegation — DPA annex + order form flowdown clarification
messages:
From: Evan Blake <evan.blake@atlascloud.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlascloud.io; legal-ops@atlascloud.io
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor delegation — initial change notice

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our procurement checklist, Atlas needs a formal flowdown for the new log-aggregation vendor that will touch customer-identifiable telemetry. Please see the attached Atlas_Subproc_List_v2.xlsx — the vendor (LogWave) will be added as a subprocessor under our Order Form, and our security team is asking for: a) the DPA annex that explicitly lists LogWave, b) proof of SOC-type evidence or self-attestation, and c) confirmation that Redwood's MSA order form carries the same retention and deletion guarantees.

We also attached a copy of the draft OrderForm for reference. Can you confirm the expected approval path and whether Redwood requires any legal redlines on our standard cascade (we typically push a 3rd-party flowdown with identical data-residency clauses)?

Appreciate a quick note on timing — procurement has a go-live window in early July.

Best,
Evan
AtlasCloud — Senior Procurement Manager

Attachments: Atlas_Subproc_List_v2.xlsx, OrderForm-2026-05-AtlasCloud.docx

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evan Blake <evan.blake@atlascloud.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor delegation — initial change notice

Hi Evan — thanks, received. Looping in Legal (Kim) and Contracts (Jonas) to triage. Quick answers up front:

- We can add LogWave to the DPA annex. We typically require the vendor to accept our standard subprocessor clauses or provide SOC2 Type II evidence and a completed security questionnaire.
- For order-form flowdown, Redwood's MSA has a standard "cascade" clause; if Atlas needs a stricter residency carveout we'll need to note that in the annex and run an escalation for an Order Form exception.
- Timeline: legal redline + evidence intake usually takes 7–10 business days if DocSign and evidence are provided promptly.

Kim — can you confirm whether the attached OrderForm language will require conditional edits to the MSA or whether we can handle purely within a DPA annex? Jonas — please advise on the procurement hold/cutover implications if we require an exception.

Thanks,
Steph

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Partnerships & GTM Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 21 May 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Subprocessor delegation — initial change notice

Stephanie / team — reviewed the attachments and did a first-pass redline of Redwood_DPA_Annex (attached). High level notes:

1) Add LogWave to Annex A (subprocessor inventory) and include a scope statement limited to "telemetry ingestion and short-term aggregation for debugging and metrics". Avoid copying Atlas's generic "logs" descriptor — be specific to limit scope creep.

2) Data residency: Atlas asked for EU-only retention in some pockets. Our standard approach is to offer a contractual commitment for in-transit and at-rest encryption and to confirm we will not transfer Atlas PII outside agreed regions except where processors operate. If Atlas insists on contractually binding EU residency for specific data classes, we'll need to raise to Product/Infra for operational feasibility.

3) Evidence: request SOC2 + encryption attestation from LogWave. If unavailable, require a completed security questionnaire and an ISO-style audit window (quarterly reviews).

4) Order Form carveouts: the Order Form includes a clause for "third-party processors" but it's phrased broadly. Recommend an addendum to the Order Form rather than changing the MSA — that reduces risk to other customers.

I'll prepare a tracked PDF and proposed language that Steph can share with Atlas. Jonas — I'll flag any procurement gating if we require a residency exception.

Kim
Lead Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Annex_v3_redline.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 27 May 2026 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Subprocessor delegation — initial change notice

Thanks all — quick ops note for scheduling: if Atlas requires the EU-only residency carveout for the telemetry subset, we will need a short procurement hold to provision a VPC-level control or a dedicated processing enclave for that workload. That provisioning lead time is ~6 weeks from sign-off. If Atlas can accept the DPA annex plus LogWave's SOC2 evidence within the standard shared infra, we can keep to the July go-live.

Action items:
- Steph: share Kimberly's redline and the proposed Annex A with Atlas, request SOC2 evidence from LogWave. (Due: 2026-05-31)
- Evan / Atlas: confirm whether they need contractual EU residency for the telemetry subset or if Annex-level commitments are sufficient.
- Marissa / Partnerships Ops: document a rollback plan if LogWave onboarding is delayed.

I'll also prepare a short procurement note for Atlas explaining tradeoffs (time vs. dedicated enclave).

Jonas
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
